Categories.value: People with flowers in Germany|Pyrography|Personality rights warning|Obermaiselstein|Alpine flora|Self-published work|Sitting young women|With consent|Sitting boys|Wreaths in Bavaria|Mothers and sons in Germany|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Young women with headbands|People in rooms in Germany|Images from Wiki Loves Folklore 2025|Images from Wiki Loves Folklore 2025 in Germany|Images from Wiki Loves Folklore 2025 to check|Uploaded via Campaign:wlf-de|Tradition der hochalpinen Alpwirtschaft im Allgäu|Almabtrieb in Swabia (Bavaria)|Featured pictures from Wiki Loves Folklore 2025

ImageDescription.value:
In the Alpine region of Bavaria, Germany, the Almabtrieb (cattle drive) or Viehscheid (in the Allgäu) refers to the process of driving cattle from mountain pastures (alps) down to the valley below. There, the animals are separated according to their owners and returned to the farm stables for the winter. Depending on the regional climate, the Almabtrieb takes place between mid-September and mid-October and is often accompanied by ceremonial customs.

If an alpine pasture has survived the summer without any accidents involving animals or people, the herd is allowed to wear a headdress. The headdress, called a wreath, is elaborately crafted from twigs and flowers and is one of the highlights of the Almabtrieb (cattle drive). The most beautiful and strongest cattle are selected for the wreathed cattle and led in front of the herd.

If an alpine pasture experiences accidents during the mountain summer, the cattle leading the way carries a wooden plaque with the name of the pasture burned into it. This plaque is also decorated with flowers. Shortly before the end of summer 2024, the Allgäu experienced a severe winter storm. The Freiburg Alpe in the Lochbach Valley, managed by Anna Zeller and Thaddäus Milz, was also affected. One animal died. Anna (pictured) and Thade were only allowed to decorate the head of the wreath cow with a plaque.

Categories.value: PD US Government|PD US Army|173rd Airborne Brigade Combat Team|Parachute training|CC-PD-Mark|Featured pictures of people of the United States|Featured pictures from the United States Armed Forces|Paratroopers of the United States|Men in swimming pools|173rd Airborne Brigade Combat Team in Italy|Featured pictures of soldiers

ImageDescription.value: A U.S. Army paratrooper assigned to the 173rd Airborne Brigade, performs wet silk training at a swimming pool in Caserma C. Ederle, Italy, March 26, 2025. This exercise is part of deliberate water airborne operation familiarization training before an upcoming jump at Lake Garda, Italy. The 173rd Airborne Brigade is the U.S. Army's Contingency Response Force in Europe, providing rapidly deployable forces to the United States European, African, and Central Command areas of responsibility. Forward deployed across Italy and Germany, the brigade routinely trains alongside NATO allies and partners to build partnerships and strengthen the alliance. (U.S. Army photo by Paolo Bovo)
